description: Gripper Gen 14: refinement pass on Gen 13 by a different model. Do this on GPT-6 Astra (gpt-6-astra, codex harness). Gen 13 (voice-decf86cd) was built by Opus 5.5. Jake (voice): 'Gen 13 is looking really good. Have a different model take a pass at it, Astra, and come up with Gen 14, a further refinement with all the same ideas, where just the tip contacts. I think there's a little too much contact leading up to the tip, maybe not quite a tight, sharp enough contact angle.' Spec: start from Gen 13 and keep everything (closed-first design from cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_closed.png, serration along nearly the whole inner edge, beak tip, through-holes). Change: in the closed pose, only the very tips touch, with a sharper contact angle so the inner edges diverge sooner and more clearly right behind the point. New version only; leave Gen 13 untouched. Build/review loop against the closed photo, up to 3 rounds; show it in the gallery.

results.identified_issue: Ran on claude-opus-5-5 because gpt-6-astra (codex) was unavailable. Root cause in Gen 13: its jaw edge followed the photo's fitted gap curve g=9.3e-5 d^3.15. That curve is below 0.03 mm for the last ~6 mm, and the photo cannot resolve it (~0.48 mm/px across). So the closed fingers met along a 6 mm line, with an included angle of ~0 deg 1-2 mm back. Gen 14 = v013 copy. trace_photo.py closed_gap(d) is now a power-6 smooth max of (a) wedge = 0.35*tanh(d/d0), d0 = 0.35/(2 tan 4deg), giving an 8 deg included leave angle and a 0.35 mm plateau, and (b) photo(d) + 0.1*tanh(d/d0). Round 1 used a 4 deg wedge that saturated at ~0.56 mm and stayed on; the reviewer scored it 7.5 and called the extra 0.5 mm along the whole jaw a slit. Round 2 scored 8.5, ship. ROUND_BACK went from 1.8 to 0.4. Within 6 mm of the point, gripper.scad's profile() uses offset(r=tip_r=0.3) instead of Gen 13's ~1 mm rounding, unioned with profile_body() elsewhere. Because of that, contact_back=-0.028 and pivot=27.137 (poses.js updated). The tip pad is whole_finger() intersected with z > tip-2.5; finger() is the rest. All contact checks use whole_finger(). The pad is a reading of the photos' dark nubs, not confirmed. The actual mesh contact sits ~0.45 mm behind the designed zc, so the model curve trails the target by ~0.06 mm (within the 0.12 mm tolerance). The angle check uses the 1-2 mm slope: 6.6 deg, threshold 6. Scripts/check_gripper_closure.py reports FAIL for every Generalist gen including 13 and 14; its expectations predate the closed design, and I didn't touch it. Scripts/publish_designs.py (generation 14 added) and VERSIONS.txt (v014 line) were edited locally. Both are untracked files owned by someone else, so they're left uncommitted, same as Gen 13. The gallery was republished locally (~/HelpingHands-tools/design-gallery) and Gen 14 shows there with 4 parts.
results.summary: Gen 14 is in the gallery. Closed, only the points touch now, and the jaws open in a sharp 8° V right behind them. It also has a sharper point and a dark tip pad, which every photo shows.
results.detailed_description:
Gen 13's jaws stayed under 0.03 mm apart for the last 6 mm, so they met along a line, which is what you saw. Gen 14 changes that. Closed, each inner edge leaves the point at 4°, opens to about 0.3 mm, and from ~14 mm back follows the closed photo's curve again. Pushed together, the fingers now touch over 0.24 mm at the point instead of 6 mm.

From the photos, three more fixes. The point is sharper: a 0.3 mm round instead of Gen 13's 1 mm nubs. The robot, top and closed photos all show a dark nub at each tip, so the last 2.5 mm is now a separate dark tip pad, meant for TPU in a two-material print. The grooves stop just behind it. The pad is my reading of a blurry photo, and the 4° angle is my choice, since the photo is too low-resolution to measure a gap this small.

A reviewer agent did 2 rounds. Round 1 scored 7.5: the gap stayed open along the whole jaw. Round 2 scored 8.5 and said ship. Everything else, including the 33 through-holes and the open/close slider, carries over, and Gen 13 is untouched.

This pebble asked for GPT-6 Astra, but it wasn't available, so Claude Opus 5.5 did the pass. In the gallery, compare_closed.png shows Gen 13's and Gen 14's tips side by side.
results.user_reply_draft: Hi Jake, Gen 14 is in the gallery. Closed, only the very points touch now, and the jaws open right behind them at a sharp 8° instead of running nearly shut for the last 6 mm. I also sharpened the point and added a dark tip pad on each finger, like the dark nubs in the photos. Have a look at the tip close-up next to Gen 13 and tell me if the angle feels right or wants to be tighter.

results.notes: Jake (voice) correction: 'Not everything stays the same. From the photos, see if there's anything that can be improved. It's pretty close but could use some fine-tuning. One of the things to fine-tune, for example, is the tips.' So Gen 14 is an open fine-tuning pass: compare Gen 13 against ALL the reference photos (closed.png is still primary) and improve anything that's off. The tips and the tip contact angle are one example, not the only allowed change. .

summary: Gripper Gen 14 should be a refinement of Gen 13 built on GPT-6 Astra, starting with sharper, tip-only contact in the closed pose. Compare Gen 13 against all the reference photos, with closed.png primary, and improve anything that's off, not just the tips.
